ZBR-2846.name: [Bargain Chemist] Toniq Stock Sync Process
ZBR-2846.description: What the discussion was about: The team met to solve inventory stock on hand discrepancies causing issues at checkout. The core problem is inventory drifting out of sync between Tonic (source of truth) and Shopify, especially around new product creation and a lack of visibility/reporting when mismatches occur. Current/existing processes: 1) New product flow today (where it breaks): Product is created in Tonic first. Zyber's process polls Tonic APIs to grab stock on hand. That attempt fails because the product doesn't exist in Shopify yet. Later when the product is approved and pushed via Tonic Eshop link integration, it appears in Shopify but inventory sync does not automatically re-trigger. 2) Locations / multi-store enablement: Historically, new products were added to Shopify only for South Island Dark Store. Gurdeep has now implemented a solution so additional locations get added automatically. 3) Ongoing inventory sync (every 15 minutes): There is a job that runs every 15 minutes per store/location that asks Tonic for stock changes since last check then updates Shopify inventory and the portal/local database at the same time. This is changes-only. Tonic often times out / errors. 4) No periodic full reconciliation. Key blockers: 1) No reliable trigger/event after product appears in Shopify. 2) Tonic API limitations (no direct get stock by SKU/PLU). 3) No reporting/alerting for mismatches. 4) Operational ambiguity + documentation gaps. Proposed solutions: Best-case (depends on Tonic) Tonic provides endpoint for stock by PLU/SKU. Option A: Trigger from Shopify new product created. Option B: Trigger from Tonic product updated. Fallback workaround. Manual workaround. Next steps: 1) Escalate to Tonic. 2) Sam to scope and document. 3) Internal escalation. Backend Developer Brief: Toniq to Shopify Inventory Update Documentation - need comprehensive documentation including Overview, API Details, Data Flow, Error Handling.

ZBR-2925.name: [Bargain Chemist] AI Product FAQs
ZBR-2925.description: Developer Brief: Scope & Implement Product-Level FAQ Generation Workflow (Search Demand → Approval → Shopify Publish). Project goal: Build a structured pipeline to generate product-level FAQs driven by real search demand, with a human approval gate, and publish approved FAQs to Shopify product pages in an SEO-friendly, server-rendered way. Core workflow: Search demand (GSC + GA4 internal search) → Google Sheet (review + approval) → Shopify publish (metaobjects/metafields) → PDP renders FAQs (+ structured data). Success criteria: Attribute queries to products (GSC by URL; GA4 internal search via search-term → clicked product mapping). FAQs generated as drafts and do not publish without approval. Publishing writes to Shopify in structured format (metaobjects preferred). PDP shows FAQs server-side, optionally emits FAQPage JSON-LD. Cap FAQs per product. Exclusion rules: never generate/publish for products with product type _pharmacist-only. Constraints: Shopify Plus store; Metaobjects available; AWS middleware exists (EC2-based); GA4 tracking implemented; No GA4→BigQuery; ~20k SKUs. Architecture: Data ingestion jobs (AWS) pulling GSC + GA4; Processing layer with filtering, clustering, draft FAQ creation; Approval & publishing via Google Sheet UI; Theme rendering via Liquid + JSON-LD. Phases: Phase 0 Discovery; Phase 1 MVP with limited products; Phase 2 expand data + AI clustering. Guardrails: no hallucinations, fact pack from Shopify only, claims risk flag, hard block on _pharmacist-only.

ZBR-2931.name: [Bargain Chemist] GA4 Search Tracking Implementation
ZBR-2931.description: Frontend Development Brief: GA4 Tracking for Boost Search Result Clicks (Storefront + Global GTM). Background: GA4 currently records internal searches via view_search_results with the search_term parameter. However, we do not have a reliable event for when a user clicks a product from Boost search results. This blocks internal search success reporting and prevents clean mapping of search demand to product pages (for downstream FAQ/SEO workflows). We already have: Global GTM container loading on all storefront pages; Existing custom dataLayer work on the storefront. Objective: Implement GA4-compatible ecommerce tracking for Boost internal search results on /search?q=...: Capture search term from URL (q parameter); Fire a GA4 ecommerce event when a product is clicked in search results: select_item; Include the associated: search_term, item_list_name = Search results, items[] payload. Page Context: Search results page format: /search?q=search+term; Boost renders results dynamically (assume AJAX re-rendering; implement with event delegation). Event: select_item (Required) - Trigger: User clicks a product tile/link in Boost search results on /search. DataLayer push format: window.dataLayer.push({ ecommerce: null }); then push GA4 ecommerce event with required fields event, search_term, ecommerce.item_list_name, ecommerce.items[0].item_id, ecommerce.items[0].item_name. Recommended fields: product_id, variant_id, sku, item_brand, item_category, price. Search Term Capture from URL param q. Product Data Capture (Boost Results): Use data-* attributes (data-product-id, data-variant-id, etc.). Item ID Convention: align with existing GA4 ecommerce setup (Shopify-style composite IDs). Click Listener Implementation: Use event delegation due to dynamic rendering. QA Plan: Validate in GTM Preview + GA4 DebugView. Edge cases: Special characters in query, Empty query / no results, Mobile results layout. Deliverables: Storefront JS implementation, Boost template updates, evidence of tracking, short documentation.
